query:
Who made the argument that natural Beaujolais wine is currently being overlooked by drinkers in the UK, and what in their phrasing correctly identifies them as the source?

Options:
A. Felix
B. Marcus
C. Kezia
D. Dom
context:
[1] (about=Dom, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Increased volume this week, legs and conditioning both intense. Body will need calories Sunday. Happy with whatever wine, red preferably.
[2] (about=Felix, core, t4 @2025-09-15T19:09:00) The Lapierre was a good choice. The lamb and the wine worked well together. The orange from Georgia was less predictable than expected, in a positive sense.
[3] (about=Felix, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Suggests 2022 Lapierre Beaujolais if Marcus has it; that producer has been consistent for five years. Questions whether it can be kept cool enough given the venue.
[4] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Wants to open a Beaujolais from France; thinks natural wine people sleep on Beaujolais, some of the best skin-contact work in France is happening there.
[5] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Has the Lapierre Beaujolais. Cellar stays cool. Also thinking an orange wine from Georgia to start, aromatic and savoury, pairs with squash.
[6] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) 2pm is perfect. Wine is sorted. If anyone wants to bring flowers or something for the table that would be nice but not required.
[7] (about=Marcus, said_by=Zara, profile, t2 @2025-09-08T19:03:30) Zara is on board with the menu and asks about the wine situation.
[8] (about=Zara, episodic, t2 @2025-09-08T19:08:00) Marcus the squash and tomatoes sound literally perfect, I'm so on board with the menu 🌿 what's the wine situation though, this is important
agent_answer: Marcus (B). His phrasing — “natural wine people sleep on Beaujolais” — is the claim that natural Beaujolais is being overlooked; “sleep on” means overlook or ignore it.
